performed_via_github_app.name: boring-cyborg
performed_via_github_app.description:
A Github bot to automatically label PRs, issues and perform all the boring operations that you don't want to do.


![Using Boring Cyborg Probot to add new labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaxil/boring-cyborg/master/assets/usage-screenshot-1.png)

![Congratulate user on first merged PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaxil/boring-cyborg/master/assets/usage-first-merged-pr.gif)

## Features

* Add labels based on the path of the file that are modified in the PR.
* Welcome new users to your project when they open their first Issue/PR or first merged PR by an
automated comment. 
* Insert Issue (Jira/Github etc) link in PR description based on the Issue ID in PR title.
* Verifies if commits/PR titles match the regular expression specified
* Check if a branch is up to date with the master when specific files are modified in the PR. This is helpful when you desire the changes to be applied sequentially, for example, alembic migrations.

## Usage

1. **[Configure the Github App](https://github.com/apps/boring-cyborg)**
2. After installing the Github app, create `.github/boring-cyborg.yml` in the default branch to enable it
3. It will start scanning for pull requests within few minutes.

```yaml
##### Labeler ##########################################################################################################
# Enable "labeler" for your PR that would add labels to PRs based on the paths that are modified in the PR.
labelPRBasedOnFilePath:
  # Add 'label1' to any changes within 'example' folder or any subfolders
  label1:
    - example/**/*

  # Add 'label2' to any file changes within 'example2' folder
  label2:
    - example2/*

  # Complex: Add 'area/core' label to any change within the 'core' package
  area/core:
    - src/core/*
    - src/core/**/*  

  # Add 'test' label to any change to *.spec.js files within the source dir
  test:
    - src/**/*.spec.js

##### Greetings ########################################################################################################
# Comment to be posted to welcome users when they open their first PR
firstPRWelcomeComment: >
  Thanks for opening this pull request! Please check out our contributing guidelines.

# Comment to be posted to congratulate user on their first merged PR
firstPRMergeComment: >
  Awesome work, congrats on your first merged pull request!

# Comment to be posted to on first time issues
firstIssueWelcomeComment: >
  Thanks for opening your first issue here! Be sure to follow the issue template!

###### IssueLink Adder #################################################################################################
# Insert Issue (Jira/Github etc) link in PR description based on the Issue ID in PR title.
insertIssueLinkInPrDescription:
   # specify the placeholder for the issue link that should be present in the description
  descriptionIssuePlaceholderRegexp: "^Issue link: (.*)$"
  matchers:
    # you can have several matches - for different types of issues
    # only the first matching entry is replaced
    jiraIssueMatch:
      # specify the regexp of issue id that you can find in the title of the PR
      # the match groups can be used to build the issue id (${1}, ${2}, etc.).
      titleIssueIdRegexp: \[(AIRFLOW-[0-9]{4})\]
      # the issue link to be added. ${1}, ${2} ... are replaced with the match groups from the
      # title match (remember to use quotes)
      descriptionIssueLink: "[${1}](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/${1}/)"
    docOnlyIssueMatch:
      titleIssueIdRegexp: \[(AIRFLOW-X{4})\]
      descriptionIssueLink: "`Document only change, no JIRA issue`"

###### Title Validator #################################################################################################
# Verifies if commit/PR titles match the regexp specified
verifyTitles:
  # Regular expression that should be matched by titles of commits or PR
  titleRegexp: ^\[AIRFLOW-[0-9]{4}\].*$|^\[AIRFLOW-XXXX\].*$
  # If set to true, it will always check the PR title (as opposed to the individual commits).
  alwaysUsePrTitle: true
  # If set to true, it will only check the commit in case there is a single commit.
  # In case of multiple commits it will check PR title.
  # This reflects the standard behaviour of Github that for `Squash & Merge` GitHub
  # uses the PR title rather than commit messages for the squashed commit ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
  # For single-commit PRs it takes the squashed commit message from the commit as expected.
  #
  # If set to false it will check all commit messages. This is useful when you do not squash commits at merge.
  validateEitherPrOrSingleCommitTitle: true
  # The title the GitHub status should appear from.
  statusTitle: "Title Validator"
  # A custom message to be displayed when the title passes validation.
  successMessage: "Validation successful!"
  # A custom message to be displayed when the title fails validation.
  # Allows insertion of ${type} (commit/PR), ${title} (the title validated) and ${regex} (the titleRegexp above).
  failureMessage: "Wrong ${type} title: ${title}"

###### PR/Branch Up-To-Date Checker ####################################################################################
# Check if the branch is up to date with master when certain files are modified
checkUpToDate:
  # The default branch is "master", change the branch if you want to check against a different target branch  
  targetBranch: master
  files:
  # File paths that you want to check for
  # In this example, it checks if the branch is up to date when alembic migrations are modified in the PR.
  # It helps avoid multiple heads in alembic migrations in a collaborative development project.
    - airflow/migrations/*
    - airflow/migrations/**/*
    - airflow/alembic.ini
```

All the features are optional. Simply add the config for the feature you want to use.

If you are having issues with the GitHub app not working, please create an issue on https://github.com/kaxil/boring-cyborg/issues.

body:
I'd like to take this one.

The cause is that `_collect_relatives` in `airflow-core/src/airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/routes/public/task_instances.py` writes its results straight back into `normal_task_ids` / `mapped_tasks_tuples`. With both flags set, the upstream pass runs first and grows those sets, so the downstream pass then starts from the selected task's ancestors as well and picks up their other descendants — `other` in your example.

The fix is to run both directions from a snapshot of the originally requested tasks and take the union, which is what the `dag_run_id is None` branch in the same function already gets from `dag.partial_subset(include_upstream=..., include_downstream=...)`. I'll add a regression test built from the Dag in your report that clears `a` with both flags and asserts `other` is not selected. PR shortly.

issue.title: Fix clearing with upstream and downstream selecting unrelated tasks

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Clearing a task instance for a specific Dag run with both `include_upstream` and `include_downstream` also selected tasks that are neither upstream nor downstream of the selected one. In a Dag whose branches share a root, it selected the whole run (#73710).

`post_clear_task_instances` collects relatives through the nested `_collect_relatives`, which passed `normal_task_ids` / `mapped_tasks_tuples` to `find_relevant_relatives` and then added the results back into those same sets. With both flags set the upstream pass runs first, so the downstream pass started from the selected tasks *and* their ancestors, and returned every descendant of those ancestors.

This PR takes a snapshot of the selected tasks before either pass and gives both passes that snapshot, so each direction is computed from what the caller asked for and the results are unioned. That is also what the `dag_run_id is None` branch of the same function already gets from `dag.partial_subset(include_upstream=..., include_downstream=...)`. Mapped tasks (`(task_id, map_index)` tuples) go through the same snapshot. Single-direction clears were already correct and are unchanged.

The regression test builds the Dag from the report (`root >> a >> b`, `root >> other`) and dry-runs a clear of `a` with each flag combination. With both flags, `main` returns `a, b, other, root`; with this change it returns `a, b, root`. The upstream-only and downstream-only cases are in the same parametrization and pass either way.

Tested locally:

- the new test: 3 passed; with the source change reverted, the both-flags case fails
- `test_task_instances.py`: 349 passed
- prek on the changed files: all hooks pass except `generate-openapi-spec`, which needs the CI image; I ran its script directly instead and the generated spec is unchanged, as expected for a change inside the handler body

closes: #73710

issue.title: Fix clearing with upstream and downstream selecting unrelated tasks

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
### Why closes: #73710 Clearing a task in a specific Dag run with both **Upstream** and **Downstream** enabled (the Clear dialog, or `POST /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/clearTaskInstances` with a `dag_run_id`) also selected tasks that are neither upstream nor downstream of it. The upstream tasks were added to the selection first, and the downstream lookup then started from that grown selection. So it also returned every other descendant of the upstream tasks. With the issue's Dag (`root >> a >> b`, `root >> other`), clearing `a`: | | upstream lookup | downstream lookup | selected | |---|---|---|---| | `main` | from `{a}` → `root` | from `{a, root}` → `a, b, other` | `a, b, other, root` | | this PR | from `{a}` → `root` | from `{a}` → `b` | `a, b, root` | Clearing with only Upstream or only Downstream was not affected. The same flaw exists in two separate places, one for Dags without a loop and one for Dags with a loop, so this PR fixes both. ### What this PR changes **1. Dags without a loop** (`post_clear_task_instances`) - **Problem:** clearing a task in a Dag whose branches share a root selected the whole run, and clearing one map index (`a[0]`) selected every map index of `a`. - **Fix:** both `find_relevant_relatives` lookups start from the requested tasks, and their results are merged only after both have returned. **2. Dags with a loop** (`select_loop_clear_scope`, added in #74349) - **Problem:** in any Dag that contains a loop, the route skips fix 1 and passes the selection to `select_loop_clear_scope`, which had the same flaw. So the issue's Dag plus an unrelated loop still selected `other`. For a task inside a loop with an upstream task outside it, the downstream walk from that outside task reached every iteration and every iteration's gate. Clearing a task in iteration 1 then replaced iterations 1 and 2, including the selected task, and re-ran the loop from iteration 0. Mark as success/failed on a task inside a loop uses the same function, and changed every iteration. - **Fix:** the selection is recorded before relatives are walked, and both directions walk from it. How a relative is matched to its execution (iteration, map index, other loops) is unchanged; it is now applied to the right starting set. Both paths now follow the rule Airflow already uses when clearing without a `dag_run_id` (`partial_subset`) and when marking a task in a Dag without a loop: `selected ∪ up(selected) ∪ down(selected)`. ### Before and after Rows 1–3 are fixed by part 1, rows 4–7 by part 2. `@N` is the loop iteration. Screenshots are at the end. | # | Dag | Action (Upstream + Downstream) | `main` | this PR | Test | Screenshot | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `root >> a >> b`, `root >> other` | clear `a` | `root, a, b, other` | `root, a, b` | T1 | S1 | | 2 | `start` fanning out to three `extract >> transform >> load` pipelines | clear `transform_sales` | the whole run | `start, extract_sales, transform_sales, load_sales` | | S2 | | 3 | row 1 with `a` mapped over 3 inputs | clear `a[0]` | `root, a[0], a[1], a[2], b, other` | `root, a[0], b` | T1 | S3 | | 4 | row 1 plus an unrelated loop | clear `a` | `root, a, b, other` | `root, a, b` | T1 | S4 | | 5 | row 3 plus an unrelated loop | clear `a[0]` | `root, a[0], a[1], a[2], b, other` | `root, a[0], b` | T1 | S5 | | 6 | `start >> report`, `start >> loop >> finish`, loop body `prepare >> [process, audit] >> combine`, 3 iterations | clear `process@1` | every task of iterations 0–2 and `start, report, finish`; iterations 1–2 are replaced and the loop re-runs from iteration 0 | `start, prepare@1, process@1, combine@1, gate@1, finish`; iteration 2 is replaced | T2 | S6 | | 7 | same as row 6 | mark `process@1` as failed | every task of iterations 0–2 and `start, report, finish` | `start, prepare@1, process@1, combine@1, gate@1, finish` | T3 | S7 | Each test fails on `main` and passes with this PR: - **T1** `test_clear_with_upstream_and_downstream_excludes_unrelated_tasks`, parametrized unmapped/mapped × without a loop/with an unrelated loop. - **T2** `test_loop_upstream_and_downstream_scope_excludes_other_descendants_of_upstream_tasks`, which also checks that only the iteration after the selected one is replaced. - **T3** `test_loop_mark_with_upstream_and_downstream_excludes_unrelated_tasks`. ### Edge case: setups and teardowns when clearing a task inside a loop For a task inside a loop, the Clear dialog clears that exact execution, and in that mode setups are not paired with their teardowns (`include_setups_and_teardowns=False`, from #74349). Take a loop body `setup >> work >> teardown >> final` and `setup >> side >> final`, and clear `side@1` with both options (S8): - `main` selects `setup, side, final, gate, work, teardown`. - This PR selects `setup, side, final, gate`. `teardown@1` was selected only through the flaw fixed here, together with the unrelated `work@1`, and Upstream only already leaves it out. Pairing setups with teardowns for exact loop selections is a separate decision, so this PR leaves it unchanged. Clearing by task id still pairs them, and bodies where the teardown runs after every task that uses the resource are not affected. ### Why this does not introduce a regression - **Single-direction clears and marks are unchanged.** Both paths start from the same input as before. - **With both options, the selection can only shrink.** What is dropped is the descendants of upstream tasks that are not relatives of the selected task, plus what they brought along: their setups and teardowns, and the later iterations their loop gates replaced. Apart from the edge case above, nothing that has to be cleared is dropped. - **One existing test asserted the old behaviour.** The `upstream=True` case of `test_outside_predecessor_selects_all_mapped_loop_occurrences` (from #74349) expected one map index inside a loop, cleared with both options, to select every task instance of the run. It now expects the predecessor, the selected map index and that iteration's gate. - **No API surface change.** Request/response models, the generated OpenAPI spec, the path without `dag_run_id` and the UI code are unchanged. - **No compatibility handling is needed for part 2.** Loops have not been released: there is no 3.4 tag, and during the 3.4.0 betas `v3-4-test` is fast-forwarded from `main` (#74327). A backport to `v3-3-test` would take only part 1, because that branch has no loop code. ### Testing - Unit tests T1–T3 and the updated test above. All 8 cases pass with this PR. Without part 2, the 5 cases with a loop fail and the 3 without one pass. - Suites run locally in Breeze (Python 3.11, SQLite, one at a time): core DB tests `API` (4141 passed, 13 skipped), `Always` (1894 passed, 3 skipped), `CLI` (673 passed) and `Core` (3517 passed, 43 skipped, 1 xfailed), and the route test file again on the final code (509 passed). The remaining suites `breeze verify` lists (core DB `Other` and `Serialization`, core non-DB tests, the `common.compat` and `fab` providers, and the docs build) are not expected to be affected and are left to CI. - Static checks through prek on the changed files: all pre-commit and manual-stage hooks, including ruff, ruff-format and mypy (`airflow-core`, `devel-common`), plus OpenAPI spec generation (spec unchanged). - Manual testing in Breeze (`breeze start-airflow --dev-mode`): rows 1–7 and the edge case, through the Clear and Mark-as dialogs (S1–S8). Rows 4–7 were also checked through the API, on `main` and with this PR.
Screenshots **S1**: row 1, clearing `a` **S2**: row 2, clearing `transform_sales` **S3**: row 3, clearing `a[0]` **S4**: row 4, clearing `a` in a Dag with an unrelated loop **S5**: row 5, clearing `a[0]` in a Dag with an unrelated loop **S6**: row 6, clearing `process` in iteration 1 **S7**: row 7, marking `process` in iteration 1 as failed **S8**: edge case, clearing `side` in iteration 1
